prompt: Input {"ranges": list of [a,b] integer pairs with a<=b}. Return how many distinct integers are covered by at least one closed range [a,b]. The result is at least the length of the longest range and at most the sum of all range lengths; [] -> 0.
Input {"s": string made only of the characters ()[]{} }. If s is balanced, return the maximum nesting depth (empty string -> 0); otherwise return -1. A balanced result never exceeds len(s)/2.

Input {"s": string of lowercase letters}. Return its run-length encoding: for each maximal run of one character, the character followed by the run length in decimal (e.g. "aaab" -> "a3b1"). Decoding the result must give back s exactly; "" -> "".
Input {"m": square matrix of integers (list of rows), possibly empty}. Return the matrix rotated 90 degrees clockwise. The result has the same size and contains exactly the same multiset of values.
Input {"nums": integer list, "target": integer}. Return [i, j] with i<j and nums[i]+nums[j]==target, choosing the smallest i and then the smallest j; return [] if no such pair exists.

Input {"nums": integer list}. Return the same values reordered by decreasing frequency; values with equal frequency appear in increasing order, and equal values stay together. The result is a permutation of nums.
Input {"words": nonempty list of lowercase words (a word may be empty)}. Return the longest common prefix of all words. The result is a prefix of every word.
Input {"s": a valid Roman numeral in standard subtractive form for a value between 1 and 3999}. Return its integer value (between 1 and 3999).
Input {"n": integer 1..3999}. Return n as a Roman numeral in standard subtractive form, using only the letters I V X L C D M. Reading the result back as a Roman numeral must give n.

Input {"m": rectangular matrix of integers (list of rows), possibly [] }. Return its elements in clockwise spiral order starting at the top-left. The result contains every element exactly once (rows x columns values).

Input {"intervals": list of [start,end] integer pairs with start<end, half-open [start,end)}. Return the minimum number of rooms needed so that no two overlapping meetings share a room. The result is between 0 and the number of intervals, and at least 1 if there is any interval.

Input {"s": string}. Return true if s is a valid dotted-decimal IPv4 address: exactly four parts separated by dots, each part 0..255 written in decimal digits without leading zeros (except "0" itself). Any character other than digits and dots makes the answer false.

Input {"nums": integer list}. Return the next lexicographically greater permutation of nums; if nums is already the greatest permutation, return the smallest one (sorted ascending). The result is a permutation of nums.

Input {"nums": strictly increasing integer list, "target": integer}. Return the index of target if present, otherwise the index where it would be inserted to keep the order. The result i satisfies 0<=i<=len(nums), nums[i-1]<target if i>0, and target<=nums[i] if i<len(nums).

Input {"nums": nonempty list of positive integers, each at most 1000000}. Return [g, l] where g is the greatest common divisor of all values (an integer) and l is their least common multiple written as a decimal string. g divides every value and every value divides l.

Input {"text": lowercase words separated by single spaces (possibly empty), "k": integer >= 1}. Return the k most frequent words, by decreasing count, ties in alphabetical order; return fewer if there are fewer distinct words. Every returned word occurs in text and appears once.

prompt: Input {"s": string}. Return the number of non-empty substrings of s (counted by position) that read the same forwards and backwards. The result is at least len(s) and at most len(s)*(len(s)+1)/2.

Input {"n": nonnegative integer, "base": integer 2..36}. Return n written in that base using digits 0-9 then lowercase a-z, with no leading zeros ("0" for zero). Reading the result back in that base must give n.

Input {"tasks": list of uppercase letters, "n": nonnegative integer}. Each task takes one unit of time; two equal tasks must be separated by at least n units (idle units allowed). Return the minimum total time. The result is at least len(tasks), and equals len(tasks) when n is 0.

Input {"data": an integer or a list whose elements are integers or nested lists of the same kind}. Return a flat list of all integers in left-to-right order. The result contains exactly the integers of data (same multiset, same total sum).
